Application Materials.content:
**With your online application you will need to provide:**
1. A copy of your degree certificate and transcripts. If your degree certificate or result is pending, please upload any interim transcripts or provisional certificates.
2. A copy of your IELTS certificate, or evidence of an accepted equivalent. Please include the date of your expected test if this qualification is pending. If you have alternative acceptable evidence, such as an undergraduate degree studied in the UK, please supply this in place of an IELTS.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Applicants need to have achieved **a 2:2 honours degree in a relevant subject area such as engineering, mathematics, or science**, or **an equivalent international degree**.
- For applicants from China: postgraduate taught applicants are required to have **a relevant four-year bachelor's degree from a recognised institution, with grades of approximately 80% or above**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
- A copy of your IELTS certificate with an overall score of **6.5 with 5.5 in all subskills**, or evidence of an accepted equivalent. Please include the date of your expected test if this qualification is pending.
- If you have alternative acceptable evidence, such as an undergraduate degree studied in the UK, please supply this in place of an IELTS.
- Find out more about [English language requirements](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/international/english-language-requirements/postgraduate).
- Applicants who require a Student visa to study in the UK must present an [acceptable English language qualification](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/international/english-language-requirements/postgraduate) in order to meet UKVI (UK Visas and Immigration) requirements.

Program Overview.content:
Data Science and Analytics (MSc) is offered full time over **17 months** with a **January start**. The course equips students with a theoretical understanding and practical experience of applying methods drawn from data science and analytics, developing in-demand skills for extracting and handling “big data” and applying modelling tools to help businesses and government organisations make better decisions. On completion, students will be well placed to progress into roles in data-intensive industries or a related research career.
The degree falls under the umbrella of the [Data Science Academy](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/data-science-academy) (DSA), run by the School of Computer Science and Informatics in partnership with the School of Mathematics, and benefits from the shared knowledge and skills of both Schools. The degree is run by the School of Mathematics.
Key features include:
- A cross-disciplinary network of experts across the School of Mathematics, the School of Computer Science and Informatics, and other University research groups.
- Professional work placements and projects with leading data science practitioners in the UK and abroad.
- Project-based learning using real-world datasets and problems.
- Teaching in the newly-built flagship building Abacws.
The programme structure includes 100 credits of compulsory modules, 20 credits from optional modules, and a 60-credit project which will typically involve working with a company on a problem of real importance. Teaching uses a mixture of lectures, seminars, computer workshops and tutorials; programming skills and relevant software packages are taught in dedicated computer suites. Industry experts are often invited to give presentations.
For the dissertation project, students are allocated three supervisors, usually two academic staff members with an interest or specialism in the student’s field of research and a sponsor supervisor from the organisation worked with during the project. Students are also allocated a personal tutor within both the School of Mathematics and the School of Computer Science and Informatics.
The programme develops programming skills, data handling and extraction skills, machine learning and informatics skills, problem solving and modelling skills, communication skills, teamwork, and logical and analytic thinking. Graduates have gone on to work with companies and Government organisations including the Office for National Statistics, Lloyds Banking Group, Nationwide, British Airways, Network Rail, UK Government, The Financial Times, Virgin Media, Welsh Water and Admiral Insurance.
An important feature of the MSc programme is the project dissertation, allowing students to apply the methods and skills acquired in the taught programme to either a real-world or more theoretical problem. This might involve working with an external company or organisation; in previous years students have worked with Admiral Insurance, Lloyds Banking Group, the Office for National Statistics and the National Health Service.

Curriculum.content:
**Duration:** 17 months - January start
**Mode:** Full time
#### Course structure
The modules shown are an example of the typical curriculum. Final modules will be published one month ahead of your programme starting.
#### Year one
You will undertake all 20-credit compulsory modules (100 credits in total) and choose a further 20 credits from a list of carefully selected optional modules. The 60-credit project will typically involve working with a company on a problem of real importance.
| Module title | Module code | Credits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dissertation | MAT099 | 60 credits |
| Applied Machine Learning | CMT307 | 20 credits |
| Computational Data Science | CMT309 | 20 credits |
| Foundations of Operational Research and Analytics | MAT021 | 20 credits |
| Foundations of Statistics and Data Science | MAT022 | 20 credits |
| Research and Communication Skills | MAT028 | 20 credits |
Optional modules for year one:
| Module title | Module code | Credits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data Visualisation | CMT218 | 20 credits |
| Databases and Modelling | CMT220 | 20 credits |
| Statistics and Operational Research in Government | MAT007 | 10 credits |
| Healthcare Modelling | MAT009 | 10 credits |
| Stochastic Search and Optimisation | MAT061 | 20 credits |
| Time Series | MAT508 | 10 credits |
The University is committed to providing a wide range of module options where possible, but module choice may be limited in certain circumstances, including limited places, minimum student numbers, prerequisites, core or required modules, and timetable clashes.
We teach using a mixture of lectures, seminars, computer workshops and tutorials. Programming skills and the use of relevant software packages will be taught in dedicated computer suites.
We will allocate three supervisors to you for your dissertation project. Usually your supervisors will be two members of academic staff with an interest or specialism in your field of research and a sponsor supervisor from the organisation you will work with during your project. You should meet regularly with your supervisor throughout your project.
An important feature of the MSc programme is the project dissertation. This allows you to apply the methods and skills acquired in the taught programme to either a real-world problem or a more theoretical problem. This might involve working with an external company or organisation.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The living costs shown are estimates for 2025/26 and are intended to give an example of living costs for a student at university; actual living costs will vary.
Estimated living costs for **postgraduates from outside the UK/EU living in University accommodation** - based on an en-suite room in Talybont North:
| Item | Per month | Per year (52 weeks except Halls cost which is 51 weeks) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rent including bills (calculated over 51 weeks) | GBP 734.16 | GBP 8,809.86 |
| Food, toiletries and laundry | GBP 283.75 | GBP 3,404.96 |
| Study costs (books and copying) | GBP 18.00 | GBP 216.00 |
| Socialising and leisure | GBP 162.50 | GBP 1,950.00 |
| Clothes | GBP 32.00 | GBP 384.00 |
| Mobile phone and TV licence (assuming a TV licence is bought for each bedroom) | GBP 19.64 | GBP 235.68 |
| Total | GBP 1,250.04 | GBP 15,000.50 |
For private accommodation, the estimated postgraduate living costs are:
| Item | Per month | Per year (52 weeks) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rent in private sector | GBP 500.00 | GBP 6,000.00 |
| Utility bills (gas, electricity, water and broadband) | GBP 106.50 | GBP 1,278.00 |
| Food, toiletries and laundry | GBP 283.75 | GBP 3,404.96 |
| Study costs (books and copying) | GBP 18.00 | GBP 216.00 |

A private housing contract is normally for a minimum of 12 months. The average rent cost included has been calculated from a search of local agents for a 4 bedroom shared house. Costs are correct as of May 2026.
No travel costs have been included in the above figures. For international students, the minimum cost of living as recommended by UKVI for studying outside London is **£1,023 per month**. To pass the maintenance test for your student visa, you will have to show you have money for living costs of **£9,207**.

Financial Aid.content:
- The Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship is available to eligible students studying on selected Postgraduate Taught degree programmes; a full list of eligible postgraduate programmes is [available online](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/documents/2873144-vice-chancellors-international-scholarship-eligible-postgraduate-courses-january-2026). Programmes not shown in this list are not included in the Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship scheme.
- For MSc Data Science and Analytics, applicants must submit their application to the University by **3 December 2025**.
- Applicants must accept their offer and pay their deposit by **10 December 2025** unless their deposit deadline is after this date, in which case the deposit must be paid by the initial deposit deadline and the offer accepted within 14 days of it being made. Deposit deadline extensions past **10 December 2025** will not be accepted for scholarship purposes.
- Conditional offer holders for MSc Data Science and Analytics must meet all offer conditions, including any English Language conditions, by **17 December 2025**.
- No separate application for the scholarship is required. If you are holding an offer for an eligible programme and meet the criteria set out in the terms and conditions, you will automatically be awarded the Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship upon enrolment.
- The Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship is a **£3,500 award**; the award may be **£6,000 or £10,000** in selected countries. It is applied to students entering into year 1 of a programme and to the first year of study only.
- The scholarship is awarded as a **tuition fee discount only** and cannot be used in place of any required deposit. No cash alternative is available.
- Scholarships of **£3,500** will be awarded to students domiciled in listed countries including USA, India, Malaysia, Singapore, South Korea, United Arab Emirates and others. Scholarships of **£6,000** will be awarded to students domiciled in Cyprus, Egypt, Greece, Jordan, Kenya, Mexico, Pakistan and Taiwan. Scholarships of **£10,000** will be awarded to students domiciled in Bangladesh or Nigeria.
- The Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship is for entry into Cardiff University in **January 2026 only** and cannot be used any other year of entry.
- Applicants who are in receipt of any other scholarship, bursary, funding or discount will not be eligible for this Scholarship.
- The Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship is available for full-time and Cardiff campus-based taught programmes only, and applicants must be confirmed as an Overseas Student for fee-paying purposes.
- The Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship is only available to **self-funded students**. If you are in receipt of funding consisting of either tuition fees or tuition fees and living costs from an external body which will be invoiced by the University for fees, such as Government, charity or a private organisation, you are not eligible for the Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
4.4 A formal offer of study is only valid for the stated programme of study and start date.
#### 5. Start dates and deferred entry
5.1 The date of entry to the programme applied for is confirmed in the formal offer.
5.2 Before applying, applicants may apply for any available intake, which may include deferred entry.
5.3 After an application has been submitted, or after an offer of study has been made, applicants may request to defer their application/place for up to **12 months from the start date of the programme originally applied for**. Approval of the deferral is not guaranteed. Applicants wishing to defer entry for more than **12 months from the start date of the programme** are required to reapply.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
When applying for most programmes if you do not have your English language test results you can send these in later. Please indicate on your application form when you took or expect to take the English language test and when you expect to receive your test results. You can then send in your test results once you have them. In this case, your offer will be **conditional upon us receiving your test results**.
In some cases students may be made offers to attend [pre-sessional English courses](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/international/english-language-programmes/pre-sessional-summer-courses) instead of or in addition to an English Language qualification or test, and some courses will require you to provide your English language results when submitting your application.
